_comment: doc 08 §8 — the save half of the persistence tunables, owned by doc 08. Landed 2026-08-19 with the SaveService/SaveManager unification: before it, the retention ladder and the quarantine cap were constants inside `sim/persistence/save_manager.gd` and the shell's slot layer had no policy at all. `sim/persistence/save_policy.gd` is the only reader; `SaveManager` and `game/save_service.gd` both take a `SavePolicy` rather than reading this file themselves, so a test can hand either one a hand-built policy without touching the disk.
_comment_catchup: doc 08 §2.12's performance budget, RE-RULED 2026-09-03 (report 98 §58, RR-160/RR-161) onto the axis it belongs on. Wave 17 (RR-133) implemented the budget as `max_coarse_hours`, a second clamp on the CREDITED ABSENCE: at the measured 5.488 ms/hour it shipped as 360 game-hours = 6 REAL hours, so hours 7-9 of a night paid nothing (doc 92 §55 measures the bill: $281,319 instead of $354,830 for an eight-hour night on a settled L3 city). A performance budget bounds how long the catch-up VEIL takes; it may never bound what the player is paid for being away. `max_coarse_hours` is therefore DELETED — from this file, from SavePolicy and from CatchUpPlanner's signature — and the budget below is a wall-clock gate on the veil.

catchup._comment_measurement: `measured_coarse_ms` is ONE FULL-band coarse hour on the FOUNDING city (data/starter_city.json) on the reference workstation: `godot --headless -s res://tools/profile_sim.gd -- --coarse-hours=48 --fine-hours=1 --repeats=3 --no-profile` -> 5.488 ms/hour. `bench_coarse_ms` is the same measurement on tests/fixtures/bench_city.json (1,500 buildings) -> 165.493 ms/hour. Both are RECORDED, not shipped: neither is what the budget is measured against, because a per-hour cost times a cap is an estimate and this block now carries the measurement itself. The Fold multiplier is doc 13 §2.13's 3-5x on top of every figure here.
catchup._comment_rule: THE GATE, and it compares two wall-clock numbers with no arithmetic in between: `veil_ms_at_cap` is the MEASURED wall clock of a whole 12-real-hour catch-up plan on the settled reference city (`tools/measure_offline_night.gd --absences=12 --settle-hours=180 --seeds=1337` -> 6,432 ms over 719 coarse hours = 8.95 ms/hour, doc 92 §55.6), and `veil_budget_ms` is what that is allowed to be. `tests/test_catchup_veil_budget.gd` asserts `veil_ms_at_cap <= veil_budget_ms` and asserts that NOTHING in sim/ or game/ reads either number — a performance budget that can reach the player's wallet is how RR-133 happened, and the structural half of the fix is that this pair is a gate and not a tunable. When the gate fails the answer is a cheaper coarse hour (doc 92 §55.7 AC-19-1), never a smaller credit.
catchup._comment_bench: The benchmark city does NOT meet the budget: 116,882 ms for the same plan (doc 92 §55.6). That is filed as AC-19-1 against the coarse step, and it is not new — at the deleted `max_coarse_hours = 360` the same city already spent 64,552 ms, because the clamp was derived from the founding city's 5.488 and had no idea the benchmark city existed. A clamp that produced 3 s on one city and 65 s on another was never bounding a veil.

save._comment_version: `current_schema_version` is the ENVELOPE version (doc 08 §2.8), and it is 1, not §8's illustrative 7: no generation file has ever shipped, so there is no history to have laddered through. It is duplicated here for documentation and asserted equal to `SaveManager.CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` by `tests/test_save_manager.gd` — a tripwire, never a source. The ladder itself is code (`SaveManager.LADDER`), because a migration step is a function.
save._comment_paths: `slot_path` is a TEMPLATE now that the shell's player-facing slots each own a generation ladder: `%d` is the slot index. Doc 08 §2.5's `user://saves/slot0/` is the same shape with the index spelled out. `device_settings_path` is device-scoped and NEVER migrated (report C-03).
save._comment_retention: Doc 08 §2.7: at most 6 unpinned + 2 pinned. The age array has SIX entries because slot A is the active generation itself (age 0 by definition); `SaveManager` consumes entries B..F as the minimum real-seconds age each history slot must clear. B newest-other · C ≥30 min · D ≥6 h · E ≥24 h · F ≥7 days. Shortening the array shortens the ladder; it may never be longer than `max_unpinned_generations`.
